Wikimedia Commons" ![bg right:38% vertical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Hubble2005-01-barred-spiral-galaxy-NGC1300.jpg?width=960) ![bg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/HAWK-I_NGC_1300.jpg?width=960) # Bars, resonances and secular evolution $$\kappa^{2}=R\frac{d\Omega^{2}}{dR}+4\Omega^{2}$$ $$\Omega_p=\Omega\mp\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\ (\mathrm{ILR/OLR}),\quad\Omega_p=\Omega\ (\mathrm{CR})$$ - Bar instability in cold disks: $t=T/\lvert W\rvert\gtrsim0.14$ (Ostriker & Peebles 1973); halos and bulges regulate it - Fast bars: $\mathcal{R}=R_{\rm CR}/R_{\rm bar}=1.0$–1.4; the Milky Way bar has $\Omega_p\approx40$ km s$^{-1}$ kpc$^{-1}$ - Orbits: $x_1$ supports the bar, $x_2$ (inside the ILR) feeds nuclear rings - Bars drive gas inwards: pseudobulges and nuclear starbursts - Near-IR light (old stars, little dust) shows the bar best (lower panel)
